events.note: Exhibited the night of 1 September 1885, on the north pier

56-foot red steel tower with occulting white light at the end of the north pier

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive record flags the light 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No'. The Historical Society says the Coast Guard operates the light. The story reports the Coast Guard's operation and does not repeat the archive's flag, which the sources do not settle.
Some accounts give 1884. Pepper says the Lighthouse Board decided in 1884 to build the light, and that it was first exhibited on 1 September 1885. The 1885 date is used.
LighthouseFriends dates the white paint to 1968. Pepper dates it to the early 1980s. Both agree the tower was red after 2009 and red in 1948. The story gives both dates.

Pepper says Ripley was made acting keeper and exhibited the light on 1 September 1885. LighthouseFriends reports a local paper announcing his arrival only on 3 October 1885 and infers a temporary keeper for the first weeks. The story states both accounts; the first-light date is the same in both.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the archive roster, Pepper and LighthouseFriends disagree. Sterritt's end date is 1934 in the roster and 1935 in LighthouseFriends. LighthouseFriends names Hutzler as keeper on 28 Feb 1929; the 1929 Bulletin names no keeper, and the roster has Sterritt in post until 1934. Not resolved; the story says so. Pepper and the roster match for Ripley (1885-1923); the roster gives his title as Principal Lighthouse Keeper, and the story uses 'keeper' because Pepper calls him the single Charlevoix keeper. Matched by name and position only where noted: the 1913 storm figure ($6,500) is for five stations together. Not read: the USCG Historian's page (archived copies would not load; a search snippet says the station was established 1914, not cited); NRHP nomination (not digitised; the NPGallery file is a placeholder); the 2004 SmithGroup historic structure report; Lighthouse Board reports for 1885 to 1890 (not in the local corpus). Newspapers: Chronicling America searches for Ripley and Charlevoix gave nothing usable for the story. Record fields to check: focal height 12.5 m and range 8.7 nm are current values, not confirmed in a source read here; characteristic 'Fl R 4s' is not cited in the story. The north-pier steel tower of 1914 has no recorded end date in the sources read. Pepper's and LighthouseFriends' pages are all-rights-reserved sites; the story uses facts in our own wording. The 1948 newspaper line is paraphrased, not quoted. Fact check 2026-10-22: the Ripley first-light dispute (Pepper vs LighthouseFriends) is now stated in the story; the 1913 storm, 1929 Bulletin, Commissioner 1915-1917 and keeper roster lines were re-read against the Bulletin PDF, the Commissioner volume and the archive page and match. Footnote 5 gives three archive.org pages of one bound volume (1915, 1916, 1917); JSON source 5 lists only the 1917 page, so the other two pages are cited in the footnote alone.
